text:
Sofia: Hi team - quick scenario: I left the company in May and took an outstanding 401(k) loan with automatic payroll repayment. I'm being rehired in September. Will my old loan repayment resume automatically when I return or is that considered satisfied/forfeited at separation? Also, I had an active limited-purpose FSA for dental in 2024 and still have some eligible expenses that I'll submit after I return. Any special steps on substantiation post-LOA?

Elliot (People Ops): welcome back if the rehire is happening! short answers: 1) 401(k) loan = depends on separation code and whether loan was paid in-full or deemed distribution. 2) limited-purpose FSA claims = usually ok if within runout; keep receipts. details below.

Tracy - Benefits: Adding details: when an employee separates, outstanding 401(k) loans are typically due. If not repaid they may be treated as a taxable distribution per plan rules. Whether the loan is "satisfied" or still active on rehire depends on the timing and the recordkeeper's policy. Some recordkeepers allow loan reinstatement on rehire within a specified window (e.g., 12 months) and can resume payroll repayments; others require a new loan application. We need to check your specific loan ID and separation code. DM me the full name + last four SSN digits and separation date and I'll open a case with the recordkeeper.

Tracy - Benefits: If your loan was treated as a distribution (i.e., you received a 1099-R), there's no outstanding balance to resume; any remaining balance was considered taxable. If it wasn't distributed and is in a pending "in-service" state, there's a chance of reinstatement.

Sofia: I did not get a 1099-R and payroll could still see deductions until my last paycheck. I left voluntarily (resignation) but it wasn't a COBRA or involuntary termination.

Tracy - Benefits: That helps. Likely it wasn't distributed, but we still need confirmation from the recordkeeper. Please DM loan ID. If it's reinstatable, Payroll will need to re-enable the loan repayment code on your rehired employee record. That can be an on-cycle change if rehire occurs before payroll cutoff. Otherwise Payroll will process it in the next run.

Payroll Bot: Note: to resume payroll deductions for a prior loan upon rehire, Payroll requires: rehired employee ID, prior loan ID, and HR/Benefits authorization. Off-cycle adjustments may be needed for missed payments.

Elliot (People Ops): for the FSA part  limited-purpose dental FSA runout: if your plan year was 2024 and you had a runout window (we have 90 days after plan year), eligible claims incurred during coverage should be submitted by the runout deadline. If you miss runout because of separation, sometimes the new vendor will allow a manual claim during conversion, but it's not guaranteed. Keep receipts and submit ASAP after rehire.

Tracy - Benefits: Also check whether you had an HSA paired with the limited-purpose FSA. HSA contributions during separation are handled differently; employer contributions stop on separation and won't be backdated. If you want us to attempt a manual employer contribution for the missed pay period, Payroll can evaluate exceptions but it's not standard.

Sofia: ok i'll DM the loan ID and save all FSA receipts. If the loan can't be reinstated and was distributed, am I able to re-loan after rehiring?

Tracy - Benefits: Yes, you can apply for a new loan after rehiring, subject to plan limits and waiting periods. If the prior loan was distributed and taxed, that doesn't block a future loan. There may be a short waiting period for plan service requirements depending on policy.

Elliot (People Ops): Action items: Sofia DM loan ID + rehire effective date. Tracy will open recordkeeper case. Payroll will check whether reinstatement is possible and advise on payroll setup deadlines. We'll update this thread with the ticket number. :white_check_mark:

Sofia: thanks all 44d I'm on it.
